reading.body:
This education and research category lists four tools that sit on opposite sides of the same academic integrity question: CheggMate and Khanmigo assist students directly with coursework and tutoring, while Turnitin AI Detection exists specifically to catch AI generated writing, meaning the category includes both the tools students use and the tools built to detect that use.

CheggMate's note explicitly flags honor code implications alongside content accuracy, an unusual pairing that names academic misconduct risk as a first order concern for a homework help tool in a way none of the other categories in this dataset do for their listed products.

Regulatory references are concentrated by age group: Khanmigo, aimed at younger students, is flagged for COPPA compliance, the law governing children's online data, while Grammarly for Education and Turnitin are flagged for FERPA, the law governing student education records generally, showing the applicable privacy law shifts with the age of the student population each tool serves.

The data does not include adoption figures, detection accuracy rates, or how schools are resolving the tension between assistance tools and detection tools within the same institution, so how these four tools actually coexist in practice is not established by this record.
